title: Minyah Dragonsister
dek: An honored operative who is still adjusting to public recognition, knows the limits of her court knowledge and chooses another mission while her sisters pursue other lives.
sources: Zarathis_Dragonsisters_NPC_Master.md — supplied 5 October 2026; quest-RP parts 024, 026, 030 and explicit evidence distinctions
body:
Minyah shares the Dragonsisters’ public honor, but she is already looking toward work beyond the celebration. Her short recorded conversation with Scribonia reveals a person still adjusting to recognition, careful about what she knows and determined to remain useful.

Honor has not changed her self-description

At the celebration on 15, Month of Cala, Year 2, Minyah waves as Captain Zythienne presents the three sisters. He honors approximately five years living among the enemy and raises them to ladies of the lands, with care promised to their families.

At the later gathering in the Month of Moirah, she accepts Scribonia’s invitation to dance, a little shy but not rude. Fine events like this are unfamiliar. She says the sisters’ work in the war has apparently earned them honor, as though the new social world is still something she is learning to inhabit.

Her modest description of herself and her sisters as lowly spies does not cancel the public elevation. It preserves the distance between work performed out of sight and the status now attached to their names.

A warrior with a mind

Minyah is preparing another mission. She tells Scribonia that she needs to get back out and use her mind as a warrior. Service remains something she wants to do after recognition, not merely an obligation that ended with the ceremony.

Kaiya separately says the sisters were given a choice about their next steps: Minyah chose work while she chose passion studies. Sheeva’s intended reprieve offers a third response. Their shared operation has not produced three identical ambitions.

The next mission’s destination, purpose, departure and outcome remain unrecovered. Preparing to go is a meaningful choice without becoming a completed adventure.

Knowing the limits of her knowledge

When Scribonia asks whether his place at the gathering has political significance, Minyah does not pretend to speak for the court. The sisters have been away a long time, she says; someone with greater social standing might know more.

That restraint matters beside her willingness to return to danger. She can be skilled and publicly honored while still unfamiliar with an institution’s private calculations.

Her exchange with Scribonia supports a courteous social connection, not an established romance. She remains close to Sheeva and Kaiya, but her age, ancestry, fuller wartime history, deeper personal relationships and later fate remain unresolved. Her shorter surviving account is not a reason to supply a future the scenes do not show.
